subject: Potential exfil detected — evidence handback & cross-border handling
messages:
From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@highbridge.co>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: security@highbridge.co
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Potential Data Exfil — request for evidence & timeline

Hi Marissa,

We detected anomalous egress from a service account that pulled a set of customer records out of our staging bucket around 2028-01-10 13:30 UTC. Initial triage suggests the files include hashed customer identifiers and partial transaction metadata for several accounts in scope.

Under the DPA (Section 8, Incident Notification & Cooperation), HighBridge needs:
- A secured snapshot of audit logs covering 2028-01-08 through 2028-01-10 (UTC)
- A confirmation of whether any Redwood subprocessors were involved in that traffic (we currently see references to "CloudEdge Inc." in the logs)
- Proposed timeline for Redwood's notification to affected data regions and any planned cross-border evidence transfers (we are EU-based for the affected customers)

Can you confirm receipt and provide a secure transfer mechanism for the snapshot? I attached an initial CSV extract (audit_snapshot_20280110.csv) with redacted IDs. We are constrained by our contract language to receive notice as soon as possible — the DPA references a 72-hour notification expectation.

Alex Moreno
Head of Security Operations, HighBridge Financial
security@highbridge.co

Attachment: audit_snapshot_20280110.csv (csv, 42KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@highbridge.co>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Potential Data Exfil — request for evidence & timeline

Alex — thanks for flagging and for the sample. Confirming receipt and opening an internal incident response path. High-level next steps from Redwood:

1) Immediate preservation: we will put a legal/ops hold on the implicated service account and preserve system-level logs (ingest, access, network egress).
2) Forensic snapshot: we can produce the audit log slice you requested (2028-01-08 -> 2028-01-10 UTC). Expect a preliminary upload within 48 hours.
3) Notification cadence: we will acknowledge publicly to your security contact within 4 hours (this email), provide a preliminary findings memo within 48 hours, and aim for a consolidated incident report within 10 business days. If contractually necessary we will shorten timelines where feasible.

A few clarification asks to avoid extra churn:
- Can you confirm the exact customer tenant IDs or the dataset labels you consider "in scope"? (Your sample is very helpful but partially redacted.)
- Do you require raw packet captures or only application-layer logs and object metadata?
- For EU-resident customer data: do you prefer evidence transfer to an EU-hosted endpoint (eu-west1) or are you OK receiving encrypted exports to your SFTP? Cross-border transfers will require coordination around our subprocessors and any required DTA/SCCs.

Operational items we are starting now: Ben will prepare the forensic checklist and secure upload instructions; Priyom is standing by to confirm subprocessor callouts (CloudEdge Inc. and TransitOps LLC).

I am attaching our internal forensic checklist (redwood_forensic_checklist_v1.docx) and will open a secure upload folder. If you prefer an SFTP handoff for chain-of-custody reasons, let us know and we'll provide credentials and key fingerprints.

We are treating this as a high-priority incident and will keep you updated as artifacts are available.

— Marissa Cole
Senior Security & Privacy Manager
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_forensic_checklist_v1.docx (docx, 18KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@highbridge.co>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Potential Data Exfil — evidence transfer options

Marissa / Alex — quick ops note:

Per Marissa's plan, we're initiating the snapshot and will stage three artifacts for transfer:
1) application audit logs (JSON)
2) object metadata export (CSV)
3) service account activity timeline (TXT)

We prefer to deliver via the secure Drive folder (link below) for faster previews, but for formal chain-of-custody we will provide an SFTP export with sha256 checksums.

SFTP details are in the attached stub. If HighBridge requires the evidence to remain entirely within EU jurisdictions, call that out now — otherwise we'll provision the default Redwood secure bucket in us-west1 and an encrypted SFTP snapshot.

Ben Carter
Incident Response, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachment: sftp_instructions.txt (txt, 2KB)
Related link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0BExampleSecureUpload

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@highbridge.co>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 12 Jan 2028 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Potential Data Exfil — contractual & cross-border considerations

Alex / team — legal here. A few points from Redwood's side to make sure the handoff is compliant with the DPA and applicable data-transfer rules:

1) Notification window — your DPA language (Section 8) requires prompt notice; we interpret that as "as soon as reasonably possible but no later than 72 hours after discovery". We will try to provide the preliminary findings within 48 hours as Marissa noted, but please be aware the 72-hour clock can be affected by (a) time to verify scope, and (b) any law-enforcement-imposed gag or preservation order.

2) Subprocessors — Priyom will confirm which subprocessors (CloudEdge Inc., TransitOps LLC) touched the data in the implicated timeframe. If evidence transfer requires engaging a third-party forensic vendor that CloudEdge or Redwood uses, we will notify you and seek mutual agreement before executing cross-border transfers of EU-resident personal data.

3) Cross-border transfers & SCCs/DTA — if HighBridge wants the raw evidence delivered to an EU-hosted endpoint or a HighBridge-controlled EU SFTP, provide the endpoint details and any DPA addendum you require. If not already in place, some transfers may need our Data Transfer Addendum (we can provision an emergency DTA/Processing Addendum for the incident). We've linked a DocuSign for an emergency processing addendum below for your review; signing will accelerate legal approval for an international transfer of forensic artifacts.

4) Evidence contents & redaction — to minimize exposure, Redwood will provide logs with technical identifiers and will accept a request for minimal redaction prior to handoff. Our standard package includes: timeline of events, object metadata (filenames, sizes, timestamps), access token mapping (hashed), and sha256 checksums for attached snapshots. Full packet captures are provided only where necessary and typically under an explicit mutual order.

Please confirm: (a) the preferred evidence transfer endpoint (Drive vs EU SFTP), (b) whether you require a specific legal addendum signed before reception, and (c) exact tenant IDs. Once we have that we will finalize custody controls and notify relevant subprocessors.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/emergency-addendum/XYZ123
